message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the family **Felidae** in the order **Carnivora**, while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the family **Equidae** in the order **Perissodactyla**.  
The most recent common ancestor of these two species is therefore the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla – in other words, the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). That ancestor lived roughly 100–120 million years ago, long before the divergence of the major mammalian lineages that gave rise to modern cats and horses.
